system:
You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
# Project Kestrel – Buyer-side review of Seller Update and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

**To:** Wattlebridge Holdings deal team
**Status:** Privileged / advice. All Seller documents treated as the other side's draft.

## 0. Threshold point – the "FINAL / settled at principal level" framing

The preamble asserts that the positions were "settled at principal level by both deal teams" and are "not intended to be re-opened." We should not accept this on the Seller's say-so. Nothing in our instructions records a principal-level agreement on caps, baskets, time limits or knowledge qualifications; the baseline we hold is price (AUD 24m), 100% of shares, debt-free/cash-free, NSW law. Please confirm with Wattlebridge principals whether anything beyond that was actually agreed. Until then, treat every "FINAL" tag as a negotiating assertion, and treat the "market context" paragraph as advocacy rather than a neutral benchmark. The market claims are also selectively framed: the ranges cited are at the seller-friendly end and ignore the standard carve-outs (fundamental warranties, tax, fraud, specific indemnities) that make such ranges acceptable in the first place.

A second structural point: the Seller Update and the Disclosure Letter contradict each other on several items (Bluefen, Riverlark, Ironquay, incident). Where they conflict, the Disclosure Letter is the document that will govern what is "disclosed" against the warranties, and it is consistently less favourable to us than the Update's summary suggests. Our mark-up should be driven by the Disclosure Letter facts, not the Update's characterisations.

---

## 1. Liability architecture (Clauses 12, 13, 9.3, 12.8, 20.5, 8.3)

### 1.1 General cap – 20% / AUD 4.8m
A 20% cap on general warranties is defensible only if it is genuinely a *general* cap with the usual carve-outs. As drafted, the Seller proposes the opposite (see 1.3–1.4). Our position: a general cap in this range is negotiable, but only as part of a package that carves out fundamental warranties, tax, the specific indemnities and fraud/wilful concealment. Given the identified issues below (Bluefen ~30% of revenue, Riverlark AUD 3.2m, a live privacy incident), we should open higher (e.g. 30–50%) and trade down against the carve-outs we need.

### 1.2 De minimis AUD 25k / basket AUD 250k (deductible)
- The basket is drafted as a true deductible ("only the excess above the basket"). Push for a tipping basket (first-dollar recovery once exceeded).
- AUD 25k de minimis is ~0.1% of price; acceptable, but ensure related claims arising from the same or similar facts aggregate for de minimis purposes.
- None of the thresholds should apply to the specific indemnities, fundamental warranties or tax.

### 1.3 Time limits – 18 months "unless expressly stated otherwise" applying to *all* Claims
The proposal that any limitation "applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise" is a drafting trap: it would sweep tax, title, indemnities and the Completion mechanics into an 18-month window. Required positions:
- General warranties: 18–24 months (18 is tolerable, but the Company's first post-Completion audit cycle should fall inside it).
- Tax warranties/indemnity: statutory limitation plus a margin (typically 7 years in Australia given ATO amendment periods).
- Fundamental/title/capacity warranties: 6–7 years or no limit.
- Specific indemnities: no limit or tied to the underlying exposure.
- Reverse the default: limitations apply only where expressly stated.

### 1.4 Fundamental / title warranties subject to general caps – reject outright
"Administrative simplicity" is not a reason to cap title. If Harbourglass does not own 100% of the shares, our loss is the whole price, not 20% of it. Fundamental warranties (title, capacity, authority, no insolvency) must be uncapped or capped at 100% of price, outside the basket/de minimis, and with a long limitation period. This is a non-negotiable for a share purchase.

### 1.5 Exclusive remedy / non-reliance applying to "all Claims of any nature"
Clauses 9.3/12.8/20.5 as summarised would exclude claims for fraud, wilful misconduct, misleading or deceptive conduct, and claims under the specific indemnities. Under NSW law an exclusion of liability for fraud will not be enforced, but the drafting still signals intent and will be used to argue the indemnities are capped. Required carve-outs: fraud, wilful default/concealment, fundamental warranties, tax, specific indemnities, and any non-excludable statutory liability (Australian Consumer Law s 18 cannot be contracted out of; a non-reliance clause only goes to causation/reliance, and should say so rather than purport to exclude all claims).

### 1.6 Buyer-knowledge qualification (Clause 8.3) – reject
This is the most damaging clause in the package. It excludes claims for anything "discoverable from the data room or public records" — i.e. constructive knowledge, extending to our advisers. Combined with the general disclosure of the entire data room (Schedule 7 / DL [1.1]–[1.2]), the effect is that nearly every warranty is pre-disclosed and the warranty package becomes close to worthless. Position:
- Delete 8.3, or limit it to *actual* knowledge of a named short list of deal-team individuals, and only of matters that are *fairly disclosed* (see 2 below).
- Expressly state that the Buyer's DD does not qualify or limit warranty claims and that the Seller cannot rely on the Buyer's knowledge as a defence except as set out in the Disclosure Letter.
- Advisers' knowledge must not be imputed.

---

## 2. Disclosure regime (Schedule 7, Disclosure Letter [1.1]–[1.4])

- **General disclosure of the whole data room and all public registers** is not acceptable. Require a "fair disclosure" standard: a matter is disclosed only if disclosed with sufficient detail to enable a reasonable buyer to identify the nature and scope of the matter. Public records disclosure should be limited to specific, dated searches (ASIC company extract, PPSR, IP Australia, court searches) listed in a schedule.
- **DL [1.4]** ("nothing admits breach, liability, materiality … or that any consent … is legally required") is fine as a no-admission clause, but it must not be read as disclosure *against* a warranty while also denying the fact is material. We should add that the Seller warrants the Disclosure Letter is accurate and not misleading by omission.
- **DL [11] "Reservation"** essentially says "we're not telling you what any of this means; work it out yourself." That is legitimate, but it confirms that the specific disclosures below are factual flags, not resolutions — which is exactly why specific protections are needed for each.

---

## 3. Specific issues – each needs a bespoke mechanism, not reliance on general warranties

### 3.1 Bluefen (DD-002) – ~AUD 3.6m / ~30% of FY26 revenue
The Update says the consent "is addressed"; the Disclosure Letter says there is **no** final written consent and **no** evidence the clause 11.3 conditions are satisfied. This is a change-of-control risk on roughly a third of revenue.
- Make a compliant, unconditional written Bluefen consent (confirming the 11.3 conditions are satisfied or waived) a **condition precedent** to Completion for the Buyer's benefit, with a form of consent agreed in advance.
- "Reasonable endeavours" is too weak — require "all reasonable endeavours" / "best endeavours" with a defined action list, Buyer participation in discussions, and a long-stop date.
- The Seller's proposal to "treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent" must be tightened: the consent must be in agreed form, unconditional, not revocable, and not conditioned on changed commercial terms.
- If Bluefen will not consent or imposes adverse terms, we need a price adjustment or walk right; consider a revenue-linked holdback or deferred consideration as the fallback.

### 3.2 Riverlark Bank facility (DD-003) – ~AUD 3.2m outstanding
A release "to be provided following Completion" is inconsistent with the agreed **debt-free/cash-free** basis and with the facility's change-of-control clause 8.1. Post-Completion we would own a company in default under a secured facility.
- Repayment and full discharge of security (clause 9.2) must occur **at or before** Completion, with the payout letter, deed of release and PPSR discharge delivered as Completion deliverables.
- Funds flow: the payout should be deducted from the purchase price and paid directly to Riverlark from the Completion funds, so Riverlark's release and our payment are simultaneous.
- Obtain a pre-Completion waiver of clause 8.1 or structure so repayment precedes the change of control.
- Add a specific indemnity for any residual Riverlark liability, break costs or unreleased security.

### 3.3 Ironquay IP (DD-004 / DD-010) – AUD 180,000 open; SOW3 Project Materials
Clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 IP on cleared payment of **every** SOW3 fee; DD-010 shows AUD 180k open; no receipt or confirmatory assignment exists. The Company may not own IP it is using. The Seller's "indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment" covers the AUD 180k only — not the loss of the IP, infringement exposure, or the cost of re-procuring the work.
- Require, as Completion deliverables: evidence of cleared payment, a confirmatory IP assignment from Ironquay to the Company, and (ideally) a direct written confirmation from Ironquay that no fees are outstanding.
- Expand the indemnity to cover all loss arising from any failure of title to Project Materials under any SOW, uncapped or capped at the full price, outside basket/de minimis/time limits.
- Back this with an uncapped IP ownership warranty (see 4 below) and an escrow/retention if Ironquay confirmations cannot be obtained pre-Completion.

### 3.4 Completion bonuses (DD-005) – AUD 420,000 not in funds flow
The Seller says these are "a matter for the Seller" but they are **conditional on Completion and continued employment** — i.e. they will be payable by the Company (our Company) after Completion, together with superannuation, payroll tax and other on-costs that the Seller pointedly does not quantify.
- Treat as Debt / Seller Transaction Costs in the debt-free/cash-free mechanics: either (a) the Seller pays them pre-Completion with evidence, or (b) the gross amount plus employer on-costs (budget ~10–12% super plus NSW payroll tax; have the accountants confirm) is deducted from the price and itemised in the funds flow.
- Add a specific indemnity for any bonus, retention or transaction-related payment to employees or advisers triggered by the transaction and not reflected in the price.
- Confirm no other transaction bonuses, accelerated equity or change-of-control entitlements exist (warranty plus schedule).

### 3.5 Data export / privacy incident (DD-006) – ~1,240 records
The Update calls this "preliminary" and "not expected to be material"; the Disclosure Letter confirms the investigation is incomplete and does not establish whether access occurred or whether notification is required. Under the Privacy Act (Notifiable Data Breaches scheme) the assessment obligation is time-limited (30 days from suspicion), and the Company may already be past that. Exposure includes OAIC notification, individual notification, customer contract notification obligations (Bluefen and Mossvale contracts should be checked for breach-notice clauses), penalties and customer churn.
- Require completion of the assessment and any required notifications **before** Completion, with the Buyer given the report and the right to approve the notification position.
- Specific indemnity for all loss (regulatory, third-party, remediation, customer claims) arising from the DD-006 incident and any related or similar pre-Completion incident, outside caps/basket/time limits.
- Privacy and data-security warranties should be given on an unqualified basis save for DD-006 as specifically described.
- Consider an escrow/retention sized to the realistic remediation and claims exposure until the incident is closed.

### 3.6 Office lease (DD-007)
Low priority, but confirm: is the notification obligation triggered by a change of control? If so, make it a pre-Completion Seller obligation and get landlord acknowledgment. Confirm no landlord consent/termination right exists.

### 3.7 Sandbar supplier renewals (DD-008, DD-011) – AUD 330,000
"Ordinary-course operating costs" is asserted, not evidenced. Three identical AUD 110k renewals, which we are told to "read together for timing/scope," suggests either a single split commitment or renewals timed around Completion. Questions for DD: are these committed, terminable, already accrued in the Accounts, and were they entered into (or renewed) in the ordinary course at arm's length? If they are new commitments between the Accounts date and Completion, they belong in the working-capital/debt adjustment or require Buyer consent under the pre-Completion conduct covenants. At minimum: a warranty that all supplier commitments are disclosed in a schedule, and a conduct-of-business covenant prohibiting new commitments above a threshold without Buyer consent.

### 3.8 Mossvale (DD-009)
The restriction is on assignment, not change of control — that is probably right, but have us check the contract directly for a change-of-control or "deemed assignment" clause rather than rely on the Seller's characterisation. If none, fine; if any ambiguity, obtain a comfort letter.

### 3.9 Title (DD-012)
A share register is prima facie but not conclusive evidence of title. We should run our own ASIC extract, PPSR search against the shares and the Seller, review the constitution for pre-emptive rights, and check for any shareholder agreements, options, convertible instruments or ESOP. Title and capacity warranties must be uncapped (see 1.4). Completion deliverables should include share transfer forms, share certificates (or cancellation), board resolutions approving transfer and registration, and resignations.

---

## 4. Tax and IP warranties – "settled under the general regime"
Not acceptable. Both need to sit outside the general regime:
- **Tax:** a full tax indemnity (pre-Completion tax, on a pound-for-pound basis), separate tax warranties, limitation period aligned to amendment periods (≥7 years), cap at 100% of price or uncapped, outside basket/de minimis. For a SaaS target confirm R&D tax incentive claims, GST on cross-border supplies, payroll tax on contractors and employee share scheme reporting.
- **IP:** given Ironquay, IP ownership warranties should be given without the general cap (or with a higher specific cap), with specific warranties on ownership of all source code, contributor/contractor assignments, open-source compliance and absence of infringement claims.

---

## 5. Price/mechanics points flowing from the above
Under the debt-free/cash-free baseline, the following should be reflected in the Completion statement / funds flow:
- Riverlark payout: ~AUD 3.2m (plus break costs/interest) – Debt.
- Completion bonuses: AUD 420k plus on-costs – Debt / transaction costs.
- Ironquay AUD 180k if the Company pays it – Debt or deducted.
- Sandbar AUD 330k – treat as Debt if committed outside the ordinary course or unaccrued.
- Consider a retention/escrow (indicatively 10–15% of price) pending Bluefen consent, Ironquay assignment and DD-006 closure, or W&I insurance with these items specifically addressed.

---

## 6. Summary of recommendations (priority order)

| # | Issue | Buyer position |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Fundamental/title warranties under general cap | **Reject.** Uncapped (or 100% of price), no basket, 6–7 yrs. |
| 2 | Buyer-knowledge / constructive knowledge (cl 8.3) | **Delete.** At most, actual knowledge of named individuals of fairly disclosed matters. |
| 3 | General disclosure of entire data room / public records | **Reject.** Fair-disclosure standard; specific searches scheduled. |
| 4 | Riverlark release post-Completion | **Reject.** Repay and discharge at Completion via funds flow; CoC waiver; specific indemnity. |
| 5 | Bluefen consent | **CP** in agreed form, unconditional; stronger endeavours; price protection/walk right. |
| 6 | Limitations applying to "all Claims" by default | **Reverse the default.** Carve out tax, fundamental, indemnities, fraud, statutory. |
| 7 | Exclusive remedy / non-reliance on "all Claims" | Carve out fraud, wilful misconduct, indemnities, non-excludable statutory claims. |
| 8 | Ironquay indemnity limited to AUD 180k | Expand to all loss from failure of IP title; confirmatory assignment as deliverable; retention. |
| 9 | Completion bonuses outside funds flow | Deduct AUD 420k + on-costs as Debt; indemnity for all transaction-triggered payments. |
| 10 | DD-006 incident "not material" | Complete assessment pre-Completion; specific uncapped indemnity; privacy warranties unqualified. |
| 11 | Tax and IP under general regime | Separate tax indemnity (≥7 yrs, 100%); IP warranties outside general cap. |
| 12 | General cap 20% / deductible basket / 18 months | Negotiable only once 1–11 are secured; push tipping basket and 24 months. |
| 13 | Sandbar, lease, Mossvale, title verification | DD follow-ups; schedule of commitments; conduct covenant; own ASIC/PPSR/constitution checks. |
| 14 | "FINAL / settled at principal level" | Confirm internally; do not accept as a constraint on the mark-up. |

**Overall assessment:** The Update presents a conventional-looking cap/basket/time-limit package, but the real transfer of risk is in the surrounding architecture — capping title, constructive-knowledge exclusion, whole-data-room disclosure, "all Claims" limitations, and post-Completion treatment of debt and consents. Taken together, these would leave Wattlebridge paying AUD 24m on a debt-free basis for a company that still carries AUD 3.2m of secured debt, an unconsented 30% customer, potentially unowned IP, an unresolved privacy incident, and AUD 420k+ of bonus liabilities — with a warranty package that is largely pre-disclosed away. Our mark-up should reorder priorities accordingly: fix the structural points (1–7) and the specific-risk mechanisms (8–11) first; the headline cap and basket numbers are the least important items on the list.

Happy to turn this into a clause-by-clause mark-up of the SPA and a response to the Disclosure Letter once you confirm the internal position on what, if anything, was actually agreed at principal level.
=== END ADVICE ===
